paragraphs: Timberland Bancorp, Inc. ("Timberland Bancorp"), a Washington corporation, was organized on September 8, 1997 for the purpose of becoming the holding company for Timberland Bank (the "Bank"). At September 30, 2025, on a consolidated basis, the Company had total assets of $2.01 billion, net loans receivable of $1.46 billion, total deposits of $1.72 billion and total shareholders' equity of $262.61 million. The Company's business activities generally are limited to passive investment activities and oversight of its investment in the Bank. Accordingly, the information set forth in this report, including consolidated financial statements and related data, relates primarily to the Bank and its subsidiary, Timberland Service Corp.

The Bank opened for business in 1915 and serves consumers and businesses across Grays Harbor, Pierce, Thurston, King, Kitsap and Lewis counties, Washington with a full range of lending and deposit services through its 23 branches (including its main office in Hoquiam). The Bank's deposits are insured up to applicable legal limits by the Federal Deposit Insurance Corporation (the "FDIC"). The Bank has been a member of the Federal Home Loan Bank System since 1937. The Bank is regulated by the Washington State Department of Financial Institutions - Division of Banks (the "DFI") and the FDIC. The Company is regulated by the Federal Reserve.

Timberland Bank is a community-oriented bank which has traditionally offered a variety of savings products to its retail customers while concentrating its lending activities on real estate mortgage loans. Lending activities have been focused primarily on the origination of loans secured by real estate, including residential and commercial / multi-family construction loans, one- to four-family residential loans, multi-family loans, commercial real estate loans and land loans. The Bank originates adjustable-rate residential mortgage loans that do not qualify for sale in the secondary market. The Bank also originates commercial business loans and other consumer loans.

The Company maintains a website at www.timberlandbank.com. The information contained on that website is not included as a part of, or incorporated by reference into, this Annual Report on Form 10-K. Other than an investor's own internet access charges, the Company makes available free of charge through that website the Company's Annual Report on Form 10-K, quarterly reports on Form 10-Q and current reports on Form 8-K, and amendments to these reports, as soon as reasonably practicable after these materials have been electronically filed with, or furnished to, the Securities and Exchange Commission ("SEC"). These reports are also available on the SEC's website at http://www.sec.gov.
The Bank considers Grays Harbor, Pierce, Thurston, King, Kitsap and Lewis counties, Washington as its primary market areas. The Bank conducts operations from:
•its main office in Hoquiam (Grays Harbor County);
•five branch offices in Grays Harbor County (Ocean Shores, Montesano, Elma and two branches in Aberdeen);
•five current branch offices in Pierce County (Edgewood, Puyallup, Spanaway, Tacoma, and Gig Harbor and another location opening soon (University Place));
•six branch offices in Thurston County (Tumwater, Yelm, two branches in Lacey and two branches in Olympia);
•two branch offices in Kitsap County (Poulsbo and Silverdale); •a branch office in King County (Auburn); and
•three branch offices in Lewis County (Winlock, Toledo and Chehalis). For additional information, see "Item 2. Properties."

Hoquiam, with a population of approximately 8,800, is located in Grays Harbor County along Washington State's central Pacific coast. Hoquiam is approximately 110 miles southwest of Seattle, Washington and 145 miles northwest of Portland, Oregon.

The Bank considers its primary market area to include six sub-markets: primarily rural Grays Harbor County with its historical dependence on the timber and fishing industries; Thurston and Kitsap counties with their dependence on state and federal government employment; Pierce and King counties with their broadly diversified economic bases; and Lewis County with its dependence on retail trade, manufacturing, industrial services and local government. Each of these markets presents operating risks to the Bank. The Bank's expansion into Pierce, Thurston, Kitsap, King and Lewis counties reflects the Bank's strategy to expand and diversify its primary market area and to become less reliant on the economy of Grays Harbor County.

Grays Harbor County has a population of 78,000 according to the United States ("U.S.") Census Bureau 2024 estimates and a median family income of $94,800 according to 2025 estimates from the Department of Housing and Urban Development ("HUD"). The economic base in Grays Harbor County has been historically dependent on the timber and fishing industries. Other industries that support the economic base are tourism, agriculture, shipping, transportation and technology. According to the Washington State Employment Security Department, the unemployment rate in Grays Harbor County increased to 5.6% at August 31, 2025 from 5.5% at September 30, 2024. The median price of a resale home in Grays Harbor County for the quarter ended June 30, 2025 increased 2.9% to $368,400 from $358,100 for the comparable prior year period. The number of home sales increased 9.2% for the quarter ended June 30, 2025 compared to the same quarter one year earlier. The Bank has six branches (including its home office) located in the county.

headings: Risks Related to Economic Conditions
Our business may be adversely affected by downturns in the national economy and in the economies in our market areas.
Monetary policy, inflation, deflation, and other external economic factors could adversely impact our financial performance and operations.
Risks Related to our Lending Activities
Our real estate construction and land loans expose us to significant risks.
Our emphasis on commercial real estate lending may expose us to increased lending risks.
Repayment of our commercial business loans is often dependent on the cash flows of the borrower, which may be unpredictable, and the collateral securing these loans may fluctuate in value.
Our business may be adversely affected by credit risk associated with residential property.
Our allowance for credit losses on loans may not be sufficient to absorb losses in our loan portfolio.
If our non-performing assets increase, our earnings will be adversely affected.
Risk Related to our Business Strategy
We may be adversely affected by risks associated with completed and potential acquisitions.
Risk Related to Market Interest Rates
Changes in interest rates may reduce our net interest income and may result in higher defaults in a rising rate environment.
Our securities portfolio may be negatively impacted by fluctuations in market value and interest rates.

An increase in interest rates, change in the programs offered by Freddie Mac or our ability to qualify for their programs may reduce our mortgage revenues, which would negatively impact our non-interest income.
Risks Related to Laws and Regulations
The level of our commercial real estate loan portfolio may subject us to additional regulatory scrutiny.
We operate in a highly regulated environment and may be adversely affected by changes in federal and state laws and regulations that could increase our costs of operations.
Non-compliance with the USA PATRIOT Act, Bank Secrecy Act, or other laws and regulations could result in fines or sanctions and limit our ability to get regulatory approval of acquisitions.
Climate change and related legislative and regulatory initiatives may materially affect our business and results of operations.
Risks Related to Cybersecurity, Third Parties and Technology
The financial services market is undergoing rapid technological changes and, if we are unable to stay current with those changes, we may not be able to effectively compete.
We are subject to certain risks in connection with our use of technology.
Our business may be adversely affected by an increasing prevalence of fraud and other financial crimes.
Risks Related to Accounting Matters

The Company's reported financial results depend on management's selection of accounting methods and certain assumptions and estimates, which, if incorrect, could cause unexpected losses in the future.
We may experience future goodwill impairment, which could reduce our earnings.

We are subject to an extensive body of accounting rules and best practices. Periodic changes to such rules may change the treatment and recognition of critical financial line items and affect our profitability.
We may experience decreases in the fair value of our loan servicing rights, which could reduce our earnings.
If our investments in real estate are not properly valued or sufficiently reserved to cover actual losses, or if we are required to increase our valuation allowances, our earnings could be reduced .
Other Risks Related to Our Business
Ineffective liquidity management could adversely affect our financial results and condition.
Our growth or future losses may require us to raise additional capital in the future, but that capital may not be available when it is needed or the cost of that capital may be exceedingly high.
Our framework for managing risks may not be effective in mitigating risk and loss to us.
We are dependent on key personnel, and the loss of one or more of those key personnel may materially and adversely affect our prospects.
paragraphs: We assume and manage a certain degree of risk in order to conduct our business. In addition to the risk factors described below, other risks and uncertainties not specifically mentioned, or that are currently known to, or deemed to be immaterial by management, also may materially and adversely affect our financial position, results of operations and/or cash flows. Before making an investment decision, you should carefully consider the risks described below together with all the other information included in this Form 10-K and our other filings with the SEC. If any of the circumstances described in the following risk factors actually occur to a significant degree, the value of our common stock could decline, and you could lose all or part of your investment. This report is qualified in its entirety by these risk factors.

Substantially all our loans are to businesses and individuals in the state of Washington. A downturn in local or regional economic conditions, as a result of inflation, rising interest rates, unemployment, recessions, natural disasters, or other adverse events, could materially affect our business, financial condition, and results of operations. Adverse economic developments in our primary market areas of Grays Harbor, Pierce, Thurston, King, Kitsap, and Lewis counties Washington, could also slow our growth, impair our customers' ability to repay loans, and otherwise negatively impact our business, financial condition, and results of operations.

Weakness in the global economy, disruptions in supply chains, and changes in U.S. trade or immigration policies could adversely affect businesses in our markets, particularly those reliant on international trade or key industries such as construction and manufacturing. These developments may exacerbate labor shortages, reduce productivity, impair borrowers' repayment capacity, increase costs, delay supply chains, lower credit demand, and heighten operational and cybersecurity risks, thereby negatively impacting our business and financial performance.
A deterioration in economic conditions in the market areas we serve could result in: •Higher loan delinquencies, problem assets and foreclosures;
•an increase in our ACL; •the slowing of foreclosed asset sales; •a decline in demand for our products and services;
•a decline in collateral values linked to our loans, thereby diminishing borrowing capacities and asset values tied to existing loans;

paragraphs: MANAGEMENT'S DISCUSSION AND ANALYSIS OF FINANCIAL CONDITION AND RESULTS OF OPERATIONS General

Management's Discussion and Analysis of Financial Condition and Results of Operations is intended to assist in understanding the consolidated financial condition and results of operations of the Company. The information contained in this section should be read in conjunction with the Consolidated Financial Statements and accompanying notes thereto included in Item 8 of this Annual Report on Form 10-K.

Timberland Bancorp, Inc., a Washington corporation, is the holding company for Timberland Bank. The Bank opened for business in 1915 and serves consumers and businesses across Grays Harbor, Thurston, Pierce, King, Kitsap and Lewis counties, Washington with a full range of lending and deposit services through its 23 branches (including its main office in Hoquiam). At September 30, 2025, the Company had total assets of $2.01 billion, net loans receivable of $1.46 billion, total deposits of $1.72 billion and total shareholders' equity of $262.61 million. The Company's business activities generally are
limited to passive investment activities and oversight of its investment in the Bank. Accordingly, the information set forth in this report relates primarily to the Bank's operations.

The Bank is a community-oriented bank which has traditionally offered a variety of savings products to its retail and business customers while concentrating its lending activities on real estate secured loans. Lending activities have been focused primarily on the origination of loans secured by real estate, including residential construction loans, one- to four-family residential loans, multi-family loans and commercial real estate loans. The Bank originates adjustable-rate residential mortgage loans, some of which do not qualify for sale in the secondary market. The Bank also originates commercial business loans and other consumer loans.

The profitability of the Company's operations depends primarily on its net interest income after provision for (recapture of) credit losses. Net interest income is the difference between interest income, which is the income that the Company earns on interest-earning assets, which are primarily loans and investments, and interest expense, which is the amount that the Company pays on its interest-bearing liabilities, which are primarily deposits and borrowings (as needed). Net interest income is affected by changes in the volume and mix of interest-earning assets, the interest earned on those assets, the volume and mix of interest-bearing liabilities and the interest paid on those interest-bearing liabilities. Management attempts to maintain a net interest margin and return on average assets ("ROA") placing it within the top quartile of its Washington State peers.

Changes in market interest rates, the slope of the yield curve, and interest we earn on interest earning assets or pay on interest bearing liabilities, as well as the volume and types of interest earning assets, interest bearing and non-interest bearing liabilities and shareholders' equity, usually have the largest impact on changes in our net interest spread, net interest margin and net interest income during a reporting period. Since March 2022, in response to inflation, the Federal Open Market Committee ("FOMC") of the Federal Reserve has increased the target range for the federal funds, which stood at 4.00% to 4.25% as of September 30, 2025. Subsequent to fiscal year end, the FOMC reduced the target federal funds rate by 25 basis points.

The provision for (recapture of) credit losses on loans is dependent on changes in the loan portfolio and management's assessment of the collectability of the loan portfolio as well as prevailing economic and market conditions. The ACL on loans reflects the amount that the Company believes is adequate to cover expected credit losses inherent in its loan portfolio. The Company recorded a provision for credit losses on loans of $853,000 for the year ended September 30, 2025, primarily due to increased loan portfolio growth. The Company recorded a provision for credit losses on loans of $1.25 million for the year ended September 30, 2024, primarily due to increased loan portfolio growth.

Net income is also affected by non-interest income and non-interest expense. For the year ended September 30, 2025, non-interest income consisted primarily of service charges on deposit accounts, gain on sales of loans, ATM and debit card interchange transaction fees, BOLI cash surrender value increases and death benefit, servicing income on loans, escrow fees and other operating income. Non-interest income is also increased by a gain on sale and net recoveries of OTTI on investment securities, if any. Non-interest income in certain periods can also be decreased by valuation allowances on loan servicing rights and increased by recoveries of valuation allowances on loan servicing rights, if any. Non-interest expense consisted primarily of salaries and employee benefits, premises and equipment, advertising, ATM and debit card interchange transaction fees, postage and courier expenses, amortization of CDI, state and local taxes, professional fees, FDIC insurance premiums, loan administration and foreclosure expenses, technology and communications expenses, deposit operation expenses and other non-interest expenses. Non-interest expense in certain periods is reduced by gains on the sale of premises and equipment and by gains on the sale of OREO. Non-interest income and non-interest expense are affected by the growth of the Company's operations and growth in the number and balances of loan and deposit accounts.

Results of operations may be affected significantly by general and local economic and competitive conditions, changes in market interest rates, governmental policies and actions of regulatory authorities.

The Company is a bank holding company which operates primarily through its subsidiary, the Bank. The Company's primary objective is to operate the Bank as a well-capitalized, profitable, independent, community-oriented financial institution, serving customers in its primary market area of Grays Harbor, Pierce, Thurston, Kitsap, King and Lewis counties. The Company's strategy is to provide products and superior service to small businesses and individuals located in its primary market area.

The Company's goal is to deliver returns to shareholders by focusing on the origination of higher-yielding assets (in particular, commercial real estate, construction, and commercial business loans), increasing core deposit balances, managing problem assets, efficiently managing expenses, and seeking expansion opportunities. The Company seeks to achieve these results by focusing on the following objectives:

Expand our presence within our existing market areas by capturing opportunities resulting from changes in the competitive environment. We currently conduct our business primarily in western Washington. We have a community bank strategy that emphasizes responsive and personalized service to our customers. As a result of the consolidation of banks in our market areas, we believe that there is an opportunity for a community and customer focused bank to expand its customer base. By offering timely decision making, delivering appropriate banking products and services, and providing customer access to our senior managers, we believe that community banks, such as Timberland Bank, can distinguish themselves from larger banks operating in our market areas. We believe that we have a significant opportunity to attract additional borrowers and depositors and expand our market presence and market share within our extensive branch footprint.

Portfolio diversification. In recent years, we have limited the origination of speculative construction loans and land development loans in favor of loans that possess credit profiles representing less risk to the Bank. We continue originating owner/builder and custom construction loans, multi-family loans, commercial business loans and commercial real estate loans which offer higher risk adjusted returns, shorter maturities and more sensitivity to interest rate fluctuations than fixed-rate one-to four-family loans. We anticipate capturing more of each customer's banking relationship by cross selling our loan and deposit products and offering additional services to our customers.

paragraphs: Timberland Bancorp, Inc. ("Timberland Bancorp"), 一間華盛頓州公司，於1997年9月8日成立，目的是成為Timberland Bank (the "Bank") 的控股公司。於2025年9月30日，按合併基礎計算，本公司總資產為2.01 十億美元，淨貸款應收款為1.46 十億美元，總存款為1.72 十億美元，總股東權益為262.61 百萬美元。本公司的業務活動通常限於被動投資活動及對其在Bank的投資進行監督。因此，本報告中所載資訊，包括合併財務報表及相關資料，主要與Bank及其子公司Timberland Service Corp有關。

Bank於1915年開始營運，為華盛頓州Grays Harbor、Pierce、Thurston、King、Kitsap及Lewis縣的消費者及企業提供全面的貸款與存款服務，透過其23家分行（包括位於Hoquiam的總行）。Bank的存款由美國聯邦存款保險公司（the "FDIC"）根據適用法律限額進行保險。Bank自1937年起為美國聯邦住宅貸款銀行系統（Federal Home Loan Bank System）的成員。Bank受華盛頓州財政機構部門-銀行分部（the "DFI"）及FDIC監管。本公司受美國聯邦儲備系統（Federal Reserve）監管。
Timberland Bank為一間社區導向銀行，傳統上為零售客戶提供多種儲蓄產品，同時專注於房地產抵押貸款的貸款業務。貸款業務主要集中在以房地產為擔保的貸款發放，包括住宅及商業/多單位建築貸款、一至四單位住宅貸款、多單位貸款、商業不動產貸款及土地貸款。Bank發放可調利率住宅抵押貸款，這些貸款不具備在二級市場出售的資格。Bank也發放商業貸款及其他消費者貸款。

本公司維護一個網站於www.timberlandbank.com。該網站上所載資訊並未包含於本10-K年度報告中，亦未經參考納入。除了投資者自身的互聯網使用費用外，本公司透過該網站免費提供本公司10-K年度報告、10-Q季報及8-K現況報告，以及這些報告的更正版本，於這些資料電子上傳至美國證券交易委員會（"SEC"）或提供給SEC後盡速提供。這些報告亦可在SEC網站上取得，網址為http://www.sec.gov。
Bank將華盛頓州Grays Harbor、Pierce、Thurston、King、Kitsap及Lewis縣視為其主要市場區域。Bank的營運從以下地點進行：
•位於Hoquiam的總行（Grays Harbor County）；
•Grays Harbor County的五家分行（Ocean Shores、Montesano、Elma及Aberdeen的兩家分行）；
•Pierce County的五家現有分行（Edgewood、Puyallup、Spanaway、Tacoma及Gig Harbor，另一個地點將於近期開幕（University Place））；
•六間分行位於 Thurston 縣（Tumwater、Yelm、兩間分行位於 Lacey 與兩間分行位於 Olympia）；
•兩間分行位於 Kitsap 縣（Poulsbo 與 Silverdale）； •一間分行位於 King 縣（Auburn）；以及
•三間分行位於 Lewis 縣（Winlock、Toledo 與 Chehalis）。有關更多資訊，請參閱 "Item 2. Properties."
霍基亞姆，人口約 8,800，位於華盛頓州中央太平洋沿岸的格雷哈伯縣。霍基亞姆距離華盛頓州西雅圖約 110 英里西南方向，距離俄勒岡州波特蘭約 145 英里西北方向。
銀行認為其主要市場區域包含六個次市場：主要為歷史依賴木材與漁業產業的鄉村格雷哈伯縣；依賴州與聯邦政府就業的湯森縣與kitsap縣；經濟基礎廣泛多元的皮瑟縣與金縣；以及依賴零售貿易、製造業、工業服務與地方政府的劉易斯縣。這些市場皆對銀行營運產生風險。銀行擴張至皮瑟、湯森、kitsap、金與劉易斯縣，反映其擴張與多元化主要市場區域的策略，並減少對格雷哈伯縣經濟的依賴。

根據美國（"U.S.")人口普查局 2024 年的估計，格雷哈伯縣人口為 78,000。根據 2025 年美國住房與都市發展部（"HUD"）的估計，該縣家庭中位收入為 94,800 美元。格雷哈伯縣的經濟基礎歷來依賴木材與漁業產業。其他支撐經濟基礎的產業為旅遊、農業、運輸、運輸與科技。根據華盛頓州就業安全部的資料，格雷哈伯縣 2025 年 8 月 31 日失業率為 5.6%，較 2024 年 9 月 30 日的 5.5% 增加。格雷哈伯縣 2025 年 6 月 30 日財季結束時，再售住宅的中位價格較去年同期的 358,100 美元增加 2.9% 至 368,400 美元。與去年同期相比，2025 年 6 月 30 日財季結束時的住宅銷售數量增加 9.2%。銀行在該縣設有六個分行（包括總行）。

管理層對財務狀況與營運成果之討論與分析，旨在協助瞭解本公司整體財務狀況與營運成果。本節所載資訊應與本年度10-K表報表第8項所附之合併財務報表及其附註一併閱讀。
限於被動投資活動與對其在銀行之投資進行監督。因此，本報告所載資訊主要與銀行之營運有關。
該銀行為社區導向銀行，傳統上為零售與企業客戶提供多樣性儲蓄產品，同時集中於以不動產為擔保之貸款業務。貸款業務主要聚焦於以不動產為擔保之貸款發放，包括住宅建設貸款、一至四戶住宅貸款、多戶住宅貸款及商業不動產貸款。該銀行發放可調息住宅抵押貸款，其中部分貸款不具備在次級市場出售之資格。該銀行亦發放商業貸款及其他消費者貸款。

本公司營運之獲利性主要取決於淨利息收入扣除信貸損失之撥備（回收）。淨利息收入為利息收入與利息支出之差額，其中利息收入為本公司在利息產生資產（主要為貸款與投資）上所賺取之收入，利息支出為本公司在利息負債（主要為存款與借款）上所支付之金額。淨利息收入受利息產生資產之數量與組成、這些資產所產生之利息、利息負債之數量與組成以及這些利息負債所支付之利息影響。管理層致力於維持淨利息邊際與平均資產回報率（"ROA"），使其處於華盛頓州同業之前四分之一。

市場利率變動、收益率曲線斜率、在利息產生資產上所賺取之利息或在利息負債上所支付之利息，以及利息產生資產之數量與類型、利息負債與非利息負債之數量與類型以及股東權益，通常在會計期間內對淨利息邊際、淨利息邊際與淨利息收入之變動產生最大影響。自2022年3月起，為應對通貨膨脹，美國聯邦儲備委員會（"FOMC"）已提高目標聯邦基金利率，截至2025年9月30日，目標範圍為4.00%至4.25%。財務年度結後，FOMC將目標聯邦基金利率調降25個基點。
貸款之信貸損失撥備（回收）取決於貸款組合之變動以及管理層對貸款組合可收回性之評估，以及現行經濟與市場條件。貸款之信貸損失撥備反映本公司認為足以覆蓋貸款組合內固有信貸損失之金額。本公司於2025年9月30日財務年度內，因貸款組合成長增加，記錄貸款信貸損失撥備為853,000美元。本公司於2024年9月30日財務年度內，因貸款組合成長增加，記錄貸款信貸損失撥備為1,250,000美元。

淨利潤亦受非利息收入與非利息費用影響。於2025年9月30日財務年度，非利息收入主要由存款帳戶服務費、貸款銷售獲利、ATM與提款卡交換交易費用、BOLI現金現金價值增加與死亡保險金、貸款服務收入、託管費用及其他營運收入組成。非利息收入亦因出售獲利及投資證券上OTTI的淨回復，若有的話，而增加。在某些期間，非利息收入也可能因貸款服務權的評價準備金而減少，或因貸款服務權評價準備金的回復而增加，若有的話。非利息費用主要由薪資與員工福利、營業場所與設備、廣告、ATM與提款卡交換交易費用、郵資與快遞費用、CDI攤銷、州與地方稅、專業費用、FDIC保險費、貸款管理與法拍費用、資訊科技與通訊費用、存款營運費用及其他非利息費用組成。在某些期間，非利息費用因出售營業場所與設備及出售OREO的獲利而減少。非利息收入與非利息費用受本公司營運成長及貸款與存款帳戶數量與餘額成長影響。
營運成果可能因總體經濟與地方經濟及競爭條件、市場利率變動、政府政策及監管當局行動而產生顯著影響。
本公司為一家銀行控股公司，主要透過其子公司銀行營運。本公司的主要目標是將銀行營運為一家資本充足、獲利、獨立、社區導向的金融機構，服務其主要市場區域格雷厄姆哈伯、皮爾斯、瑟斯頓、基斯普、金與劉易斯縣的客戶。本公司的策略是為位於其主要市場區域的小企業與個人提供產品與優質服務。
本公司的目標是透過專注於發放高報酬資產（特別是商業不動產、建設及商業企業貸款）、增加核心存款餘額、管理問題資產、高效管理費用，以及尋求擴張機會，來為股東創造回報。本公司透過專注於以下目標來達成這些結果：

在現有市場區域內擴大我們的影響力，透過競爭環境的變化所產生的機會。我們目前主要在華盛頓州西部營運業務。我們採用社區銀行策略，強調對客戶的靈活與個性化服務。由於我們市場區域內銀行的合併，我們認為社區與客戶導向的銀行有機會擴大其客戶羣。透過提供迅速的決策、提供適當的銀行產品與服務，以及讓客戶能接觸到我們的高階管理階層，我們認為像Timberland Bank這樣的社區銀行，可以在我們市場區域內與較大型銀行區隔開來。我們認為我們有機會吸引更多的貸款人與存款人，並在我們廣泛的分行網路內擴大市場影響力與市場佔有率。
資產組合多元化。近年來，我們已限制發放投機性建設貸款與土地開發貸款，轉而發放信用評分較低風險的貸款。我們持續發放所有者/建造者與定製建設貸款、多單位貸款、商業企業貸款與商業不動產貸款，這些貸款提供較高的風險調整回報、較短的到期日以及對利率變動較敏感，與固定利率的一至四單位貸款相比。我們預期透過交叉銷售貸款與存款產品，並為客戶提供額外服務，來捕捉更多客戶的銀行關係。

headings: 與經濟狀況相關的風險
本公司業務可能因國家經濟及我們營運地區經濟衰退而受到負面影響。
貨幣政策、通貨膨脹、通貨收縮及其他外部經濟因素可能對我們的財務表現及營運造成負面影響。
與我們貸款業務相關的風險
我們的不動產建設及土地貸款業務使我們面臨顯著的風險。
我們對商業不動產貸款的重視可能使我們面臨更高的貸款風險。
我們的商業貸款償還通常取決於借款人之現金流，而現金流可能難以預測，且用以擔保這些貸款的抵押品價值可能波動。
本公司可能因住宅不動產相關信用風險而受到負面影響。
本公司對貸款應收帳款之信用損失撥備可能不足以吸收貸款組閤中的損失。
若本公司非 Performing 資產增加，將會對營業收入產生不利影響。
與本公司業務策略相關之風險
本公司可能因已完成及潛在之併購相關風險而受到不利影響。
與市場利率相關之風險
利率變動可能減少本公司淨利息收入，且在利率上升環境中可能導致更高的違約率。
本公司證券投資組合可能因市場價值波動及利率變動而受到負面影響。
利率上升、Freddie Mac 所提供方案之變動或本公司符合其方案之能力，可能減少本公司房貸收入，進而對非利息收入產生負面影響。
與法律及法規相關的風險
我們的商業不動產貸款 portfolio 範圍可能使我們面臨額外的法規審查。
我們營運於高度受規範的環境，可能因聯邦及州法律及法規的變更而受到不利影響，這可能會提高我們的營運成本。
未能遵守 USA PATRIOT Act、Bank Secrecy Act 或其他法律及法規，可能會導致罰款或處罰，並限制我們取得收購相關法規核准的能力。
氣候變遷及相關的立法與法規措施，可能對我們的業務及營運成果產生重大影響。
與網路安全、第三方及科技相關的風險
金融服務市場正在經歷快速的科技變革，若我們無法跟上這些變革，我們可能無法有效地競爭。
我們在使用科技方面的應用，可能面臨某些風險。
本公司業務可能因詐欺及其他財務犯罪事件頻繁發生而受到不利影響。
會計事項相關風險
本公司所報告的財務結果取決於管理階層對會計方法及某些假設與估計的選擇，若這些假設與估計不正確，可能會導致未來出現意外損失。
本公司可能遭遇商譽減損，這可能會降低本公司獲利。
本公司需遵守大量會計規則與最佳實務。這些規則的定期變更，可能影響關鍵財務項目之處理與認列方式，進而影響本公司獲利能力。
本公司可能遭遇貸款服務權公允價值下降，這可能會降低本公司獲利。
若本公司對不動產投資的評價不正確，或未充分提列準備以覆蓋實際損失，或本公司被要求提高評價準備金，則本公司獲利可能會減少。
其他與本公司業務相關的風險
無效的流動性管理可能不利於我們的財務結果與狀況。
我們的成長或未來虧損可能需要我們在未來籌措額外資金，但該資金可能在需要時無法取得，或該資金的成本可能高得不成比例。
我們管理風險的架構可能無法有效降低對我們的風險與損失。
我們依賴關鍵人員，若失去其中一位或多位關鍵人員，可能對我們的前景造成重大且不利的影響。
paragraphs: 我們承擔並管理一定程度的風險以進行業務運作。除下列所列風險因素外，其他未特別說明或目前為管理層認為不重要之風險與不確定性，也可能對我們的財務狀況、營運成果及/或現金流產生重大且不利的影響。在做出投資決策前，您應仔細考量下列所列風險因素，並配合本Form 10-K及其他向SEC提交之文件中所包含之所有資訊。若下列風險因素中任何一種情況實際發生且程度重大，本公司普通股之價值可能下跌，您可能損失全部或部分投資。本報告內容完全受這些風險因素所限制。

我們 substantially all 之貸款係提供給華盛頓州之企業與個人。若因通貨膨脹、利率上升、失業率增加、經濟衰退、天然災害或其他不利事件導致當地或區域經濟狀況惡化，可能對我們之業務、財務狀況及營運成果產生重大影響。華盛頓州之主要市場區域，包括格雷哈伯縣、皮斯縣、瑟斯特頓縣、金縣、基斯普縣及劉易斯縣之不利經濟發展，也可能減緩我們之成長、影響客戶償還貸款之能力，並對我們之業務、財務狀況及營運成果產生其他負面影響。
全球經濟狀況惡化、供應鏈中斷，以及美國貿易或移民政策之變動，可能對我們市場中之企業造成不利影響，特別是那些依賴國際貿易或關鍵產業如建築與製造業之企業。這些發展可能加劇勞動力短缺、降低生產力、影響借款人償還貸款之能力、提高成本、延遲供應鏈、降低信貸需求，並增加作業與網路安全風險，進而對我們之業務與財務表現產生負面影響。
我們所服務之市場區域經濟狀況惡化，可能導致：•貸款違約率提高、問題資產與財產遭沒收；
•我們之 ACL 增加；•財產遭沒收資產銷售速度減緩；•我們產品與服務之需求下降；
•與貸款相關之擔保價值下降，進而降低貸款之 borrowing capacities 與現有貸款之資產價值；
